summary.headline: Clean Science Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR193 crore with 46% EBITDA margin; FY26 standalone revenue fell 12% to about INR796 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to about INR193 crore on volume recovery, with EBITDA of INR88 crore (46% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (40%), but revenue fell 19% YoY. For FY26, standalone revenue declined 12% from INR900 crore to INR796 crore, attributed to loss of an FMCG key account (4-MAP), lower offtake and pricing pressure. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 14% to about INR246 crore, led by HALS (Clean Fino-Chem), with EBITDA of INR96 crore (33%) and PAT of INR58 crore. Management said Clean Fino-Chem reached its first positive EBITDA (INR7 crore) and that the Hydroquinone/Catechol plant is still stabilising at about 10-15% utilisation.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 72% of FY26 standalone revenue. Management cited a rebound in flagship product volumes and a gross margin (RMC 33%) about 2 points better than prior quarters.

segments.name: Pharma-Agro (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 19% of FY26 standalone revenue. The pharma intermediate plant was refurbished for HALS intermediates, and the older pharma intermediate was dropped.

segments.name: FMCG (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed the balance 9% of FY26 standalone revenue. A key FMCG account (4-MAP) was lost during the year.

segments.name: HALS (Clean Fino-Chem subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4 FY26, at over 1,000 tonnes per quarter versus about 350-360 tonnes eight quarters earlier. Blended realisation was about INR460/kg versus INR420-430/kg in Q3; exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%. Subsidiary EBITDA margin was about 15% in Q4 versus about 1% in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Performance Chemical 2 (water treatment-related capex) expected to commercialise by September 2026; validation in Q3, initial commercial production in Q4, and a pickup in FY28.
Hydroquinone/Catechol plant expected to reach optimal operations in 1-2 quarters; captive HQ/catechol now replaces imports for TBHQ and Veratrole.
Capex budget for FY27 of about INR80-100 crore; Clean Fino-Chem projects under an INR200 crore enabling Board resolution, with investment likely in the second half of FY27.
Management aspires to a HALS blended realisation of USD7-7.5/kg but did not give FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance, calling FY27 a 'very tricky' year dependent on macro and crude oil.
Management said it is not pencilling in any price hikes; it expects to benefit in an inflationary environment, as it did in FY23.
capex_capacity: Clean Fino-Chem Hydroquinone/Catechol plant commissioned in December 2025; still in initial stabilisation, with utilisation about 10-15% and March 2026 HALS exit utilisation about 40%.
Performance Chemical 2 commercialisation timeline moved due to scarce manpower linked to labour movement from higher gas prices; now targeted by September 2026.
Plans to debottleneck HALS lines and add a dedicated HALS 2020 line (in-house technology, validated with European customers) and to backward-integrate further key intermediates with minimal capex.
Pharma plant refurbished in the next couple of months to produce HALS intermediates, replacing Chinese sourcing.
Subsidiary capital infusion of about INR200 crore in FY26 takes total investment in subsidiary to INR750 crore.
demand_pricing: MEHQ: management is maintaining market share by calibrating prices against Chinese hydroquinone producers, who are less affected by raw material costs. Phenol and acetone prices rose sharply, and long-term contracts (half-yearly or yearly) could not pass on increases; these will be renegotiated on expiry.

HALS demand: export share rose to about 50% in select products (Europe, Middle East, US), with Southeast Asia and LatAm being explored. Distribution partners are adding safety stock, and inbound customer interest is rising.
Anisole: management said it is the largest producer and consumer globally and India; competition from China does not affect its sales, as anisole is mainly used captively.
Base chemical prices reportedly rose about 2x in some commodities, but management said these are not transactional benchmarks. Management said China has a pricing advantage over other geographies.
Management declined to share product-wise revenue, geographic split, or product-level volumes, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HALS revenue jump sharply, and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer validation and trials delayed the response by several quarters. Exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%, with over 1,000 tonnes sold in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company passing on higher raw material costs (phenol, acetone, ammonia)?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were passed on partly, not fully; long-term contracts could not be repriced, and these are to be renegotiated as they expire. Q4 subsidiary EBITDA was INR8 crore despite March price spikes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Performance Chemical 1 (HQ/catechol) utilisation and breakeven outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 10-15%. Management expects two more quarters to optimise norms and yields before ramping utilisation further.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a volume or gross margin explanation for MEHQ, given the share-defence pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sequential growth of 7-8% was volume-led, led by flagship products. Standalone gross margin improved on product mix, with no one-off gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and the performance bonus reversal amount?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex could be INR80-100 crore, with Clean Fino-Chem investments likely in the second half. The bonus reversal was about INR11 crore.

risks_watch: Raw material and commodity volatility (phenol, acetone, ammonia, crude) and the lag in passing on costs under long-term contracts.
Pricing competition in MEHQ from Chinese hydroquinone producers and possible new capacity from Vinati Organics and Gem Aromatics in anisole, MEHQ and BHA.
HQ/catechol plant ramp-up and yield norms; utilisation at about 10-15% still needs to improve.
Performance Chemical 2 commissioning slipping further due to manpower constraints.
Standalone revenue down 12% in FY26 after loss of a key FMCG account; sustained volume recovery needs to be confirmed in Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on HALS momentum and margins, but cautious on the macro outlook and FY27, with no numerical guidance. Management was evasive on product-level data, competitor details and volume targets, citing competitive sensitivity.
key_quotes: We continue to see scale in our HALS business segment, which saw the highest ever revenue in Q4 FY26 with continued improvement in favorable product mix.
This is going to be a very tricky financial year for chemical industry in my view.
Today, we stand at 50% export in select products. So our exports have picked up dramatically.
